**Review of the landing hero draft**

**Claims check**
- "Subscribers can pause or cancel any time": matches the approved claim in the brand policy (subscription terms). Fine.
- "free UK delivery on orders over £25": matches the approved wording (shipping policy). Fine.
- "means most boxes ship free": this is a problem. The policy doesn't support it, and nothing shows what share of orders or subscription boxes come to more than £25. It is an unsourced statistic dressed up as a benefit. It also muddies the threshold: if a box costs under £25, it doesn't ship free. "Boxes" also isn't how the policy describes the products (tins and tea bags), so the word may not match what customers receive.

**Other checks**
- No superlatives, guarantees, health claims, green claims or urgency.
- Voice is warm, plain and unhurried, uses UK spelling and has none of the banned words. "Easy to stop and start" is a little loose, but acceptable as a headline-style line.
- No labels are needed for a brand-owned landing page.

**Fix:** Cut the "most boxes" claim and state the approved terms as written. For example: "Tea that's easy to stop and start. Subscribers can pause or cancel any time, and delivery is free across the UK on orders over £25."

Hold the draft until that phrase is changed. It will need Sam's approval before going public.
